definition: In statistics and related fields, a similarity measure or similarity function or similarity metric is a real-valued function that quantifies the similarity between two objects.
details: Although no single definition of a similarity exists, usually such measures are in some sense the inverse of distance metrics: they take on large values for similar objects and either zero or a negative value for very dissimilar objects. Though, in more broad terms, a similarity function may also satisfy metric axioms. Cosine similarity is a commonly used similarity measure for real-valued vectors, used in (among other fields) information retrieval to score the similarity of documents in the vector space model. In machine learning, common kernel functions such as the RBF kernel can be viewed as similarity functions.

explainer.lead: A similarity measure turns 'how alike are these two things' into a single number. It underpins retrieval, matching and ranking wherever objects must be compared.

tiers.eli5: Like a score that says how close two songs are in taste — high for near twins, near zero for totally different ones.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick a measure that matches the data and the embedding model, then rank results by the score. A common pitfall is mixing measures, such as comparing unnormalised vectors with a measure that assumes unit length.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a real-valued function of two objects, typically the inverse of a distance: large for similar objects and zero or negative for very dissimilar ones; some variants also satisfy metric axioms.

explainer.example: Cosine similarity scores two document vectors, giving a high value when the documents share vocabulary and direction.
